laws.rule: Everyone entering the Havasupai Reservation for tourism needs a valid permit bought before arrival through the Tribe's official booking system; entering without one is trespass. Third-party, resold or transferred permits are invalid. Each permit is 3 nights, 4 days; staying past 11am on the last day is trespass. Cancellations 90+ days ahead get 50% back; later, nothing.
laws.heading: Havasupai permits

laws.rule: The trip leader must check in at Grand Canyon Caverns & Inn on the start date or the day before, with photo ID matching the booking. Everyone must wear the issued wristband at all times on the reservation; vehicles parked at Hualapai Hilltop need the parking permit.
laws.heading: Havasupai check-in

laws.rule: The Havasupai Reservation is 'dry': possession, use, distribution, consumption or sale of any drugs or alcohol is prohibited. Weapons and fireworks are not allowed.
laws.heading: Dry reservation

laws.rule: Camping only in the campground (not in Supai Village, on trails, at Hualapai Hilltop or within 150 feet of waterfalls); campfires not allowed; quiet hours 8pm to 5am. Entering tribal land means consenting to the Tribe's civil jurisdiction; the Tribal Court has exclusive jurisdiction over tourism matters.
laws.heading: Campground and jurisdiction

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Stay on the main trails; residential areas and non-visitor trails are off limits. Water is sacred to the Tribe: put nothing in it that may pollute it and use biodegradable soap. Don't feed any animals.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: No photos, videos or recordings of tribal members, community members, animals, homes, buildings, burial grounds, or sacred sites and objects.
culture-and-protocol.note: From the Tribe's tourism terms and conditions.
